learningObjective: Given a GEMM followed by a pointwise chain, decide which fusion form (epilogue vs. separate kernel) is expressible and legal.

canonicalClaims.claim: Epilogue fusion of pointwise ops onto a GEMM only delivers memory-traffic savings when the compute kernel applies the pointwise chain to each output tile in registers before writing to DRAM; otherwise the fusion is logical only and offers no bandwidth benefit.
conditions: The GEMM implementation exposes an epilogue extension point (cuBLAS Lt, CUTLASS, TensorIR compute_at at the output tile).
Pointwise ops are pure and elementwise over the GEMM output.
nonImplications: Does not imply every fused pattern is faster in wall-clock; small problem sizes or downstream memory-bound ops can invert the trade-off.
Does not imply arbitrary pointwise chains are supported; libraries expose a fixed catalog.

misconceptions.claim: Any pointwise op that follows a GEMM at the IR level is automatically fused with no DRAM round-trip.
misconceptions.whyWrong: IR-level fusion is a rewrite; the physical kernel must implement the epilogue to avoid re-reading the M×N tensor.

misconceptions.claim: Broadcast biases (`[N]` shape) cannot be fused into GEMM epilogues.
misconceptions.whyWrong: cuBLAS Lt and CUTLASS support per-column bias broadcast; this is one of the most common epilogue patterns.

misconceptions.claim: Epilogue fusion is illegal when M×N is not a multiple of the warp size because the tail block violates SSA form.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Tail blocks are handled by masking or a separate epilogue tile; SSA form is unrelated to divisibility.

misconceptions.claim: Epilogue fusion always yields a wall-clock speedup because it reduces memory traffic.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The GEMM is often compute-bound; epilogue arithmetic adds work per output element, which can slightly increase kernel runtime while cutting downstream traffic — net gain depends on the pipeline.

implementationFacts: cuBLAS Lt exposes epilogue enums for bias, activation (ReLU/GELU), and scale.
CUTLASS uses an EpilogueVisitor / EVT framework for arbitrary pointwise chains at the output tile.
TorchInductor emits Triton templates with epilogue slots for matmul + pointwise fusion.
performanceScenarios: For M=N=4096, GEMM output is 64 MB in FP32; epilogue fusion of add+GELU saves one full read/write, roughly 128 MB of HBM traffic.
